summary.text: Carrie Rheingans is a Democratic member of the Michigan House of Representatives representing District 47 and is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
Carrie Rheingans's general-election opponent is Justin Griffis (R).
She previously worked as project director of the Michigan Public Health Institute and sits on the Agriculture and Families, Children, and Seniors committees.

paragraphs.text: Carrie Rheingans lives in Ann Arbor, Michigan, and earned a B.S. in German and biology, an M.P.H. in health behavior and health education, and an M.S.W. in community organization from the University of Michigan.

Her career experience includes working as project director of the Michigan Public Health Institute, interim director of human services with the Center for Healthcare Research and Transformation, and director of civic engagement with Casa Latina.
Rheingans has served on the Washtenaw County Board of Health and the Washtenaw Emergency Medical Services Commission.
Rheingans assumed office in the Michigan House on January 1, 2023, and in 2025-2026 sits on the House Agriculture Committee and the Families, Children, and Seniors Committee.

In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey, she described herself as a health policy expert, educator, and community organizer, and said she is active in American Federation of Teachers Local 6244 and serves on the board of Communities Joined in Action.
